byte placement can be complete while semantic ownership is wrong: the generic `norm` fragment owns the output residual norm, and only the op plan has the context to see the malformed object, a plane K3 never reaches today

why_this_transition_and_not_the_whole_ru: The rung has seven planes (semantics/parser, graph ownership, role classification, carrier + oracle, decode traversal, batch traversal, public lift). Only the first three can be measured on the real checkpoint today — K3's headers are in the cache, its payload is 2.8 T — and they are the planes the reconnaissance found broken or silent. The traversal planes need an oracle that does not exist yet; that oracle is the next artefact, built before any arithmetic is written, and the traversal transition gets its own freeze against the oracle's commit. Freezing the whole roadmap now would forecast baseline mechanics the oracle has not yet revealed.

the_transition.intervention: Give the attention residual its own semantic form and let the plan own and address its operands: a distinct residual-topology variant with a block size and a required exit reduction, read from the declaration or not at all; graph ownership of the output pair as one explicit object under the declaration, with the generic norm fragment no longer swallowing the output residual norm; four per-layer roles of this topology, required on every layer under the declaration and refused as strays without it; and the executor's refusal of the topology by name, read by the report through one authority, so the declaration cannot run as a single stream.
the_transition.success: K3's declaration, ownership and addressing findings move exactly as scored below, its execution-surface finding turns from representable into an honest refusal, no other row moves, the swept norm leaves the final-norm object, and the four per-layer operands classify only under the declaration.
the_transition.non_claim: No execution: no carrier, no traversal, no oracle-backed arithmetic in this transition. No g_proj (K3-REP-GATE-1), no LatentMoE (K3-LATENTMOE-1), no quantization, no vision tower. No real-payload claim now or later in the rung — the execution witness, when it comes, is synthetic by construction.

the_six_decisions_settled.1_distinct_variant: `ResidualTopology::AttentionResidual { block_size }` beside SingleStream and HyperConnection. Parsed from `text_config.attn_res_block_size` as declared or not at all — never defaulted, never inferred from the presence of `*_res_*` tensors (identity is declared, not inferred from operands). The exit reduction is part of the variant's contract: a component declaring the topology must ship the output pair.
the_six_decisions_settled.2_ownership_before_execution: one explicit object, `attention_residual_exit`, owning `output_attn_res_norm` [hidden] and `output_attn_res_proj` [1, hidden] together, placed only on a component that declares the topology (the HC head's ownership rule). The `norm` fragment stops sweeping the output norm: the exit group's fragments precede the generic norm fragment in the vocabulary, so ownership is decided by the specific rule and never by substring luck. A component that declares the topology and ships no exit pair keeps a blocking execution-surface finding naming the exit — the analogue of GLM's headless finding.
the_six_decisions_settled.3_roles_after_the_topology: four roles of this topology — the attention-site norm and projection, the mlp-site norm and projection — classified on the layer under the declaration (any operator: KDA, MLA, softmax), geometry checked at [hidden] and [1, hidden], required on every layer by closure, refused as strays on a single-stream component. Not aliases of the generic norm role.
the_six_decisions_settled.4_carrier_not_reused_blindly: deferred to the traversal transition, with the decision recorded now: the carrier's semantic type encodes history (prefix [hidden] + snapshots [history, hidden]), not streams; it may share the enter/leave site infrastructure wave 19 built, but it is not a Bundle with a different stream count.
the_six_decisions_settled.5_oracle_before_implementation: the next artefact after this transition lands, and before any Rust arithmetic: a torch transcription of `_apply_attn_res` and the block schedule at a small geometry (as scripts/hyper_connection_oracle_export.py did for HC), exporting per-site probs, mixed vectors, snapshot events and the exit, with REJECTING controls for each ordering mistake: attention-site reduction over the old snapshots before the boundary snapshot is appended; the snapshot is the entering prefix state, not the mixed vector; layer 0's attention reduction is skipped; layer 0's mlp reduction runs over one candidate; the exit reduction is mandatory; mixing over raw candidates, not normalised ones.
the_six_decisions_settled.6_synthetic_execution_witness_only: K3's headers move plan-level findings; its payload is not an execution witness and the rung will never claim one. The traversal transition's witness is a hidden-5-style substrate on an ordinary stack carrying the oracle's weights.

how_this_transition_can_be_wrong_in_a_wa: Everything here is representation: the tests can prove the declaration, the ownership and the roles agree with the headers, not that the mechanism they describe is the one the reference runs. That is the oracle's job, and the oracle does not exist until the next artefact.

The exit object's two tensors are matched by name fragments; a checkpoint that spelled the exit pair another way would be unplaced again, not mis-owned, which is the honest failure but still a failure the synthetic fixtures do not exercise.
K3's own op plan never closes in this transition, so the one place the malformed FinalNorm object would have been caught stays masked on the real row; it is exercised only on synthetic estates.
sequence_after_this_transition: oracle (torch, rejecting controls) -> freeze the traversal transition against the oracle's commit -> carrier + decode -> batch -> lift, each measured, each its own commit. Then the centre of gravity moves back to REPRESENT, residency and the K3 physical execution plan.
